speechtext: she is laid up?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: two ago.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
she do at Sorel?
Yes.
Where is she located when Located in Sorel a week or How much salvaging does

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
The salvaging is not done
at Sorel; but she is capable of doing salvage work when it is necessary.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
Has she ever done any
salvage work since her purchase?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: No.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: Has she ever been requested to do any since her purchase?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: Salvage.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: Was she used as an icebreaker to take the place of another vessel?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: Yes, but she was not an icebreaker.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
She was purchased for
$80,000 as an icebreaker, but turned out not to be an icebreaker? Is that not the fact?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
This vessel was bought to
replace another one which has been destroyed, and this one is much stronger and is capable of taking care of herself in the ice.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
Is it not a fact that she
was laid up at Midland, Ontario, during the last twelve months because she was not fit

Supply-Marine and Fisheries
to; (perform the work, for which she was intended when purchased, and that the government had to hire private tugs to perform this work?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: No.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: It is not the fact?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: No.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: Is it not the fact that after the government purchased that boat large sums of money had to be spent to get her in condition?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: Some money was spent, but not a very large amount.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: How much?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: On her boilers?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
No, generally, hull and
engines. In 1923-24 we spent $7,100.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: Was that work done by tender or by day work, and where was it done?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: By tender and contract.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: Is the minister aware that that boat was on the Atlantic in St. John harbour and was hawked all round the coast for $25,000 with no takers before the government purchased her?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: We have no such information.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: What is the wage bill on these boats that are laid up waiting for somebody to call on them for salvage work?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: For the Mikula, $39,000.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
I want to raise my protest against this wastefulness on the part of the government. This boat is laid up all summer presumably waiting to go out on a call for salvage, and the government is spending $39,000 a year for keeping people on the boat to do nothing, to eat their meals, to walk around the deck, to have a good time and, of course, to vote properly according to the expectations of the employer. That amount of $39,000 is being spent for nothing at all at a time in this country when I contend -and every reasonable man will agree with m*-that there should be no wastefulness or extravagance at all. When men are going into bankruptcy because they are being sued for their income taxes, this government keeps one boat-and I do not know how many others-tied up to a dock at an expense of $39,000 in the summer months

waiting for somebody to call on her to do salvage work, work that she has never done yet and has never been requested to do. I do not know how the minister justifies that kind of thing. Surely there must be some limit to the waste of the money of the tax-' payers of this country. Can he give any justification for such wasteful expenditure? I suppose there is a captain on the boat and he must be employed all the year round although he can be doing nothing. I suppose there will be two or three engineers, twenty men employed there all the time. This is beyond the comprehension of any reasonably-minded man, unless there is some political matter behind it.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
This vessel is not an
ordinary vessel; she cost a very large sum of money, and we must have on her a man having the necessary qualifications to look after such an expensive vessel and to keep her ready for any emergency that may arise. It is in the interest of shipping generally to have this boat ready and available in case of need.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: What is the emergency that the minister has in mind that makes it necessary to keep twenty men on board this vessel at an expense of $39,000 a year?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: I have already stated the reasons that are sufficient to keep these men on board. I am quite sure if we had not a proper number of men on board this boat with the amount of money she has cost the country, the criticism would come from my hon. friends that we were not taking care of the property of the state.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
Let us get away from
that kind of bunk. If the minister says that we are to waste thirty or forty thousand dollars for fear of a little bit of criticism from the other side, he is not showing much common sense. This boat is tied up at Sorel, and there is no likelihood of a call being made on a boat like that. Why there should be a staff of twenty men on board her, no reasonable person can understand. In all the lake ports boats costing quite as much as this boat are tied up all winter. Of course they are not expected to go out on salvage, but they do not have twenty men on board, they have two or three watchmen, caretakers, and that is all that is required. That is all that is required in this case. The smooth explanation of the minister as regards the expensive piece of machinery will not go down with people who are overburdened with taxation. The explanation of the minister is no justification at all. If he has nothing

Supply-Marine and Fisheries
better than that, why can he not get one or two more officials to give him something that will appeal a little more to the committee? What we want in this country is economy, and if the minister, being a new broom, cannot sweep a little cleaner than this, he is not giving us all that was expected of him when he was appointed. I would imagine a minister, on taking office for the first time, would try to make a record for himself, would show a desire to effect some economies in his department. This is as wasteful as anything that has ever occurred in the Marine department, and that is saying a good deal. We ought to cut $50,000 out of this item for the caretaking of boats that he has tied up at docks.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
That is really comic. I
did not think my hon. friend was capable of expressions of that kind and of contributing so much to the burlesque of the occasion.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
The burlesque is over
there.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: He tells us that when a ship at sea is in distress, this vessel would not be able to go out to aid it. If there was a crew of 84 on board and there was distress at sea, what chance would there be of her going to sea? She is tied up in Sorel, a thousand miles from the ship that is in distress.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: Sorel hurts you.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
I think my hon. friend is
himself in distress. Or perhaps he is like one of the salvage boats; he is trying to come
to the relief of the minister. But he has not succeeded very well.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: That is only your opinion.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: He has not said anything of any account, and in that respect he is only normal. I still think, notwithstanding what the hon. gentleman from Hants has said- this oracle of the Maritime provinces-

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
It is better to be a
Maritime oracle than to be writing burlesque and circulating it.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: I did not get that.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
You did not
miss anything.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: If the hon. gentleman insists upon being obscure he cannot expect me to understand what he is talking about. But his attempt to come to the rescue of the min-inster is a dismal failure.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: In your opinion.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
No, that is the opinion
of the committee.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
It is only the hon.
gentleman's opinion.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: What about taking a vote on it?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: Go ahead.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
I am not surprised at my
hon. friend's views, but he must not advocate extravagance and waste and try to excuse the government by throwing the responsibility on the preceding administration. I do not think there is any parallel at all between the record of the preceding government under normal conditions and the wasteful extravagance that is going on at the present time.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: The preceding government was never normal.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
They were normal from
1911 to 1914 when the war broke out. But perhaps the hon. member forgets that there was a war.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
I have a dim recollection of
it.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
Things became somewhat
abnormal about that time; what happened from 1914 until the present government came into power was all abnormal in the sphere of government, and there is no parallel between conditions then and conditions now. We have reached the time in this country when we simply must economize; but we are going

Supply-Marine and Fisheries
deeper and deeper into debt all the time. Our debt is increasing alarmingly, the increase this year being over $30,000,000. But notwithstanding that fact no effort is made by the government to practise economy, although in a matter of this kind there is an opportunity for retrenchment. We can cut down expenses even though someone may have to go and find another job on some other boat. This is a time when sailors should be able to find employment; it should not be necessary for them to be kept busy caretaking, waiting for a call from goodness knows where, perhaps an S.O.S. from the Isle of Wight or some place like that. This amount should be cut down.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: Before the hon. member for West Toronto worries any more about this matter perhaps he will allow an old salt water sailor to give a little information to a fresh water one.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
We have just had advice
from the hen. member for Hants (Mr. Mar-tell).

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
Well, you are a fresh water
sailor yourself. If the hon. member will permit me to go on, he can address the committee afterwards. This vessel, which is now called Mikula, was formerly known as the J. D. Hazen, having been named at that time after a celebrated politician from the province of New Brunswick, whence my hon. friend (Mr Hanson) also comes. Mr. Hazen was Minister of Marine in the Tory government from 1911 to 1917 and this vessel was built while he occupied that office. Under Mr. Hazen s regime the J. D. Hazen was built for the same purposes for which, as the Mukula, she is used at the present time; she was so engaged until she was sold to the Russian government. While she was in use under the Tory government she carried the same strength of crew, if not more men that she has now, and her expense was just the same. It amuses me to hear either the hon. member for York-Sunbury (Mr. Hanson) or the hon. member for West Toronto (Mr. Hocken), or even my genial friend the ex-Minister of Finance (Sir Henry Drayton), criticising the present administration in regard to this vessel.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
I have not
started yet.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
My hon. friend made a fair
attempt but he did not get very far. There is no question that this ship is necessary for service on the St. Lawrence. It is true that during the summer months after the ice has disappeared there is not much for her to do; 
but how could the department hope to retain her officers and crew if it hired them for only three or four months of the year during the ice breaking season? The captain of this ship is one of the best sailors in the country; I know him very well and I can inform the committee that he is one of the most experienced men in his line in Canada. I think therefore that the department is doing the right and proper thing in retaining him on salary for twelve months even although the vessel is laid up at Sorel or somewhere else waiting for a call.
The hon. member for West Toronto evidently does not understand what salvaging means; let me explain the term to him as briefly as I can. As everyone knows, the river St. Lawrence has a tortuous channel and in the summer months when the big steamers arrive from the Old Country they are apt to get into difficulties in going up the river. I think it is a wise precaution for this government as it was for the Tory government when they were in power, to keep the Mikula, or the J. D. Hazen as she was then, or the Earl Grey or some other ship in readiness to go to the relief of vessels when necessary. The fact that no salvage claims have been made is something to be thankful for, and no one complains in that respect. Shipping men and those who have goods to export from Montreal to Liverpool should be thankful indeed, in the first place, that the Mikula is ready to go to their assistance, and in the second place that there is no occasion for her to go. The very fact that no claims have to be made tends to make a difference in the insurance. A few years ago when the Empress of Ireland was sunk in the St. Lawrence by a coal boat coming from Sydney, if a boat like the Mikula had been then in readiness it is possible that a great many of the passengers would have been saved. Does my hon. friend from West Toronto suggest, in the face of that, that this boat should be laid up, her fires drawn, and the crew discharged, so that if an accident of that kind occurred there would be no ship in readiness to render assistance? Although this vessel is costing money, and possibly too much money, the fact remains that the matter is too important for us to take any chances; we cannot allow the ship to be put out of commission for the sake of saving a few dollars in wages of the crew. I say most certainly that she should be kept in 10 p.m. commission all the year round. Indeed, I think it is a mistake that she should have a crew of only twenty. If any accident occurred it would take some time to muster a sufficient force for her to proceed to the rescue. The minister is making a great

Supply-Marine and Fisheries
mistake in my opinion in keeping only twenty men on the ship.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
How long would it take
her to get ready?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: If it took her as long as it took in the case of the Niobe it would be six weeks. My hon. friend's government did exactly what he proposed a moment ago.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: But they did not buy the Niobe.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
I know they did not buy the
Niobe, but after they got her Mr. Hazen, allowed her to fall into a state of disrepair, just as my hon. friend would have the department do in this instance. The result in the case of the Niobe was that when war broke out it took six weeks to get her ready and she was obliged to return in a few weeks, her boilers having got into an unsafe condition. If that is what my hon. friend wants to happen to this ship-I do not think he does-then I am glad to make this explanation for his benefit.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
Now, Mr. Chairman, we
all see the great error made by the Prime Minister when he selected his Minister of Marine and Fisheries. The lecture we have just listened to by the hon. member for Lunenburg (Mr. Duff) demonstrates that he should be occupying the) position of the hon. member for Richelieu (Mr. Cardin). But I should like to get down to business. Is the minister serious in saying that this ship is intended as a salvage ship during the season when she is not in commission as an icebreaker, although while so maintained at Sorel less than 24 of the ordinary complement of 84 officers and men are retained? As the hon. member for Lunenburg has rightly pointed out, the only chance of the ship doing salvage work is away down the gulf or near the Newfoundland coast. In a little town like Sorel the ship could not be fully manned inside a week, and it would take her forty-eight hours to get down into the gulf. It would seem that this salvage business on its face is only a camouflage for keeping twenty men on the pay-roll-either they are too many or they are too few. I think the view advanced by the hon. member for Lunenburg is correct, that is, if the ship is intended for salvage work she should be kept in commission at a point where she can do the work without delay instead of being laid up on the mud banks of Sorel.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
Mr. Chairman, this boat is provided with the finest salvage apparatus obtainable. Not only in the gulf may salvage
work be necessary, but in the St. Lawrence channel from Montreal to Quebec, and even below Quebec. But it is absolutely necessary that we keep this vessel at a point where we can use her with the least possible delay when the occasion demands, and I think Sorel is the best place at the present time. If the boat were laid up at Quebec my hon. friends would have reason to complain of the extra cost because of the larger number of men necessary to handle the vessel on account of the tides.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
Is there
any difference between the rate of wages paid the officers in the province of Quebec, for example and in the province of British Columbia?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: The rates are a little lower in the province of Quebec. The rates in British Columbia are governed to a certain extent by the rates paid on United States vessels.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: I have no doubt that the hon. gentleman's remarks about the tremendous cost of salaries were relevant with respect to an idle salvage ship, but they might create a misapprehension. The salaries paid to these men are not high. For example, in the province of Quebec we have chief engineers pulling down $150 a month. Now, what is the average length of term of a chief engineer's job in Quebec?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
The salary of the captain
of the Mikula is $160 a month.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: That is a disgrace.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
And the chief engineer
gets $150 a month.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: Mr. Chairman, I think, as the hon. member for Lunenburg says, such salaries are a disgrace: they are not even a living wage. If we work out the chief engineer's salary on the basis of nine months, which is the general average for the province of Quebec, his annual income is only $1,350. No man can keep a family of five on such an income.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: Are they not all found?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
Then we
have the second engineer receiving, on the same basis, $1,125 a year. I protest against the department paying their officers in Quebec these wages, and then pleading as an excuse that private individuals are paying the same rate. As the minister has said, on the Pacific coast the men have a very effective union, and it is a tribute to the union that

Supply-Marine and Fisheries
they have been able to secure salaries for chief engineers at the rate of $185 per month, or $2,220 for the twelve months, which is the average term in British Columbia. I would urgently ask the Minister of Marine and Fisheries and also the Minister of Public Works (Mr. King), who, too, has a little to do with this aspect of the case, to increase the wages of their chief engineers and other technical men in their employment until they are being paid at least a living wage. The present wages in Quebec are below those necessary to maintain the recognized standard of living and are a disgrace to the government.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
Are these men employed
all the year round or only nine months?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: Chief officers are employed all the year round'.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: Then the argument of the hon. member for Bow River goes by the board.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: Not in the least. The average time for marine engineers in the province of Quebec is nine months.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: But these men are on the year round.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: The men on this particular ship are. But we can clear this up in a moment. How many chief engineers are employed the year around and how many on part time?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: Out of twenty-eight, eleven are in commission the year round.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
Are the chief engineers
paid the year round? I think that is the point.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
No.
Mr. HANSON; What is the average of those who are not in commission the year round?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: Eight months.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: Is it not true that these gentlemen, in addition to their salaries, receive a very substantial allowance? For instance, their uniforms are provided for them.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: Oh, oh.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: That is an important item; the hon. member need not sneer at it. The men are found in everything, as a matter of fact.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: This is a free house.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
But an hon. member has
no right to sneer; it is not polite.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
Put it on the ground of
civility, not right.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
It is not
necessary for me to answer my hon. friend to my right. Will the minister take my suggestion into consideration? These men really deserve more money than they are getting.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
I have already received a
petition from members of the Engineers' Association and other employees on these boats, asking that their salaries be fixed at the same rate as in British Columbia, I can assure my hon. friend that I will take the matter into serious consideration.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
I notice another item in
the estimates, a subsidy for wrecking plant, Quebec and British Columbia. Are there other salvage plants on the St. Lawrence besides the Mikula, and if so, where are they located? Does the government own any of the salvage ships in Quebec or in that vicinity?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: There is a wrecking plant at Quebec.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
Subsidized or owned by
the government?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: Subsidized.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
Is there a salvage ship
attached to that plant too?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: Yes.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: So the Mikula is not the sole salvage ship on the river? There is a sort of auxiliary? ,

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: Yes.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: A superfluity.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: Will the minister give us a few particulars about the Murray Stewart? What information had the department before buying that boat? Did they ascertain how many years she had been tied up at Quebec and St. John? What did they find1 out?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: This vessel was built at Port Arthur, and she was two or three years old when we bought her.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
Was this the
boat that was down at St. John on the Atlantic coast? I would like a plain yes or no.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
Yes.

Supply-Marine and Fisheries

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
What had she
been doing down there? What work was she in?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
We have no information
as to that.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: Is the department in a position to deny that she was tied up down there, and attempted to be sold in vain for some years?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
Having no information,
we cannot say.
Sir HENRY DRAYTON Then apparently the department bought her without knowing anything about her?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
Except that-
Sir HENRY DRAYTON. If the minister knows anything about her I am prepared to get the information.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
An examination was made
before we bought her.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: An examination of what? Here is a boat that our information says was useless, could not be got rid of for $25,000, and a politician gets her and sells her to the government for $81,000. That is our information, and I want to know if it is correct? Did the department ascertain what she had been doing, how long she had been in the market, and how long she had been tied up?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
And how long Stewart
owned her before he sold her to the government?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
That is a fair question.
She might have been towing Noah's Ark.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: She looked older than that.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
The boat was built in
1918. Mr. Stewart was the proprietor up to the time we bought her.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
What I am
trying to find out is whether the department knew what had happened to that boat from 1918 up until they bought her. Apparently she is the bid boat we knew at St. John. That is where she came from. Did the government make any inquiries at all as to what she had been down there for?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
I do not think it was
necessary to ascertain that.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: Did the minister find out when Mr. Stewart bought that boat?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: He built it himself in 1918.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
Was he still
the owner when the government bought her?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: Yes.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
I want that
plain and straight, Mr. Chairman. Was Mr. Stewart the owner from the time the boat was built until she was sold to the government?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
Yes, he was always the
registered owner.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
At any rate,
that is all the government knew about it, is it?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: Yes.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
The boat was
not working down at St. John, was she? Is Mr. Stewart not the gentleman of Toronto, of the Home Bank?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: Yes.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: Well, what did he have that boat for down at St. John?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: We have no information.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
I see. Who
valued that boat before the government paid $81,000 for her?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: The officers of the department.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: Who were they?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: The Chief Engineer, Mr. Fraser; the Commissioner of Lights and the Steamboat Inspector also made a report upon her.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
What are Mr
Fraser's initials?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
And who was
the other gentleman?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: J. G. Macphail, Commissioner of Lights.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
What was his
duty in connection with it?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: He is the Commissioner of Lights.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
Now I would
like to find out where the government took possession of that boat.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: At St. John.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
How long die
it take that boat to go from St. John tc Midland.

Supply-Marine and Fisheries

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
It is hard to answer such
a question at this late date.
Sir HENRY DRAYTON; I suppose the records will show when she began to do business?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
The minister did not
keep the log.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: But he has a very efficient deputy minister in front of him.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: Hear, hear.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: We all agree.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: The deputy minister is not in a position to answer that question.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: Does the minister know what coal alone was lost in that movement, when there were other boats up there that could have been bought easily enough?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
It is very hard to say at
this time, after two years, what it cost to take the boat up there.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: Can the minister tell us how many days that boat has been in service since she was bought? My instructions are that she was not fit for service at all, and repairs are said to have been made on her in the first instance. What work did she do the whole of the first year?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: The usual work in connection with the lights.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: What does that consist of?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
Carrying supplies to the
fights.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: Is the deputy in a position to tell his minister how many days that boat was under repair in 1923-1924 at Midland?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
The repairs were made
during the winter months.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
How long a
time did they take?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
We are not in a position
to state at the present time.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: DRAYTON: To oome back to the Mikula again. She was sold to the Russian government at about her cost to the Canadian government. Is that right?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: Yes.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
That did not
seem to be so very badly done after all. Was she in good condition when she came back?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: Yes, she was in good condition.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: What icebreaking diid she do during the season of 1923-24? When was she out? We were told she was not out at all.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
She was in commission
all the winter months.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
Did she do
anything though?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: Yes.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
Is my hon.
friend sure about that?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: Yes.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
Are the salaries and
wages of the officers and crews included in this vote?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: Yes.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
Coaling and all the
other items of expense?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: Yes.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
Where do these boats
operate in winter? They operate from January to April, but where do they operate?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
The Montcalm and the
Lady Grey operate from Quebec to lake St. Peter on the St. Lawrence.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: All the winter?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: Yes.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
Where are the supplies,
say of the Mikula, purchased? How is her coal purchased? Is that bought by tender?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: Yes.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
Are the tenders publicly
advertised for-

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: Yes.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: -or is there a patronage list in the department?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
We ask for tenders from
the different coal dealers.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: Locally, that is in Sorel?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
Not in Sorel. There is
none in Sorel, do not be afraid.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
I wonder if
we have got the whole distinction now between maintenance and repairs. How much is for maintenance and how much for repairs?

* Supply-Marine and Fisheries

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
Here are the different
items:	Total salaries, 1446,300. That is for
all the twenty-eight boats.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: Supplies?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
Board, $147,800; fuel,
$351,800; steward's supplies, $126,600; hull and engine repairs, $307,800; uniforms, $29,700; making a total of $1,500,000 for the twenty-eight boats.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: There is nothing at all in that for repairs?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: Yes, the total for hull and engine repairs is $307,800.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
Then, I think,
the minister said the boat was in commission from January to April. At what point was she working?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
Principally at Cap Rouge,
between Quebec and lake St. Peter, on the St. Lawrence.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
Was that for
the purpose of keeping a ferry running at Quebec, or what was the object?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
No, she was employed to
keep the ice from forming in the channel of the St. Lawrence between Quebec and lake St. Peter.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
Just how far
inland do we keep navigation going all the year? The general season of navigation ceases some time in December if I remember We have no sailings from Montreal or Quebec in winter. That being the case why do we do all this amount of work at that time?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
I can answer the question
if I may be allowed. The answer is, that it is to protect properties that are above St. Jean des Chaillons, what they call the Richelieu river. The frazil ice forms there, and creates a dam, and if that is allowed to continue all the property between that place and the shore of lake St. Peter is destroyed. Some years before the icebreaker was put on even the main highway was carried away, to say nothing of houses and other property. When the frazil ice forms the water rises, and when the wind is from the north or the south, the bank, and the property on it, is washed away. The icebreaking is done so as not to permit the frazil ice to form.

Item agreed to.
Examination of masters and mates, $20,000.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
It is a very important
matter to have competent officers on the ships that are operating on the Great Lakes and on 207
the St. Lawrence. I should like to find out from the minister whether examinations are still being held as they have been in the past.
I also should like to know to what class of ships the examinations apply. Are examinations held whenever candidates present themselves, or do they take place every year, and if so, at what particular time?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: The examinations are held at Halifax, Quebec, Yarmouth, North Sydney, St. John, N.B., Montreal and Prince Edward Island. For the Great Lakes division they are held at Toronto, Collingwood, Port Arthur, and Selkirk in Manitoba; and for the western division at Victoria and Nelson.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
Who is the present
admiral of the fleet. Is it the hon. member for Lunenburg (Mr. Duff) or is it the hon. member for Three Rivers and St. Maurice (Mr. Bureau)?

Item agreed to.	*
Navigation schools, $7,000.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: Where are these schools located?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
At Halifax, Yarmouth,
North Sydney, St. John, Quebec, Kingston, Collingwood and Vancouver.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
That seems a
very small amount of money t.o carry on the schools efficiently. What is the idea? What is done?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
This appropriation is to
provide for the instruction of seafaring men. and those desiring to qualify as masters and mates, under section 84 of the Canada Shipping Act. The schools at Halifax,Yarmouth and St. John are operated the whole year round. At North Sydney the school is operated for three months in the year, Quebec four months, Kingston three months. Twenty-four lectures are delivered during the winter at Collingwood by the examiner of masters and mates, and twenty-six lectures are delivered during the winter at Vancouver by the examiner of masters and mates.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: What are the sources of revenue of these schools? Are these schools maintained out of this appropriation of $7,000 a year? It has been suggested that the lecturers give their services free. Is that a fact?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
The examiner at Halifax
receives a salary of $1,860, the examiner at Yarmouth receives $800 and the examiner at North Sydney receives $360 for four months' work. At St. John a salary of $1,500 is paid for the whole year.



Supply-Marine and Fisheries

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
Who conducts the school
there?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: R. J. Pollock at St. John. The salary at Quebec is $360, and at Kingston there is a grant to a navigation school conducted by Queen's University of $500. At Collingwood Captain Cole, who gives lectures, is paid as an examiner, and the same at Vancouver.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: I am sure the ex-Minister of Finance (Sir Henry Drayton) will join with me in congratulating the minister on the good work he is carrying on with such a small amount of money. I am surprised he is able to give instruction at so many points for $7,000.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
How many weeks in the
year are these schools carried on? I would not like to have the member for Victoria and Carleton (Mr. Caldwell) think that these schools are conducted all the year round.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
I have just stated that
at Halifax and Yarmouth the schools are conducted all the year round. At North Sydney the school is conducted for four months in the year. At St. John the school is conducted the year round, and at Quebec for four months of the year.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: Many pupils?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
At Halifax there are
seventy-seven pupils, at Yarmouth thirty-seven, at St. John fifty-one, North Sydney six, Quebec forty and Kingston thirty.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: How long is the course of instruction? How long does it take a man to qualify?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: It depends on the pupil.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: The minister has some idea of the average, I presume.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
A good number of these
pupils are in a position to pass the examination after one year.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: I think the idea is that the men have to take voyages and spend a certain length of time at sea. They also get instruction. In the last ten years has there been any substantial alteration in the number of schools, or in the cost of them, or in the method of their provision?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
We are spending a larger
amount now than we have spent in the past. A few years ago the Halifax school was only conducted for a certain number of months, and the same at Yarmouth and St. John, but for a few yearn these schools have been conducted the whole year.

Item agreed to.
To provide for the temporary relief of distressed seamen, $5,000.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
How is this
work standing now? There were some difficulties from time to time in connection with it, particularly during the war period. Sailors were stranded. I take it, that this is an international service which we perform in connection with other countries, looking after the sailors of other nationalities. The money is advanced and we are supposed to get the money back. Is this a vote for that purpose?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: This is to provide only for our own people.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
AVhy is it
marked "temporary"?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: We make a collection from the owner of the vessel when we can do so.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
The money is
advanced and you hold the owner of the vessel for it. It is very much the same thing. How did it work out last year? Were we able to make our collections? How much money was advanced, and how much did . the vessel owners pay back to us? What vessels are in arrears?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: We have spent $4,666.73 for the season of 1923-24. I have all the names here. The list is very long; but unfortunately I have not the amounts.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: I never asked for the names of the sailors. Under this vote the money is supposed to be paid back to the Crown by the owners of the vessels, and we spent under it last year $4,600. I was just wondering what diligence there was in collecting it. How much have we collected from the owners of the vessels out of that $4,600 odd. That is the practical thing.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
Is this relief only for
sailors who are articled to some ship owner? Does this apply to distressed seamen who are not under contract with any ship owners, who are temporarily out of work or in ill health?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: No; this applies to shipwrecked seamen only.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
Is it not a fact that if
a crew is taken off a vessel at sea and taken to a foreign port, money is provided for bringing them back to Canada and the department usually endeavours to collect that from the owners of the vessel if they are

Supply-Marine and Fisheries
worth it? The master of the vessel is called upon to pay his own way back. I cannot understand why that should be so, but that is the old rule.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
Let the minister bring
down the information in regard to the collections later.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
We have made no collections. It should be remembered that in a good number of cases, when a vessel is wrecked, it is very hard to run after the proprietor of the vessel and make any collection.
"Sir HENRY DRAYTON: Does this information go far enough to show how many ship owners are in the happy position of not getting their bills, how many wrecks there were or whether there was a great number? The Minister of Customs and Excise suggests that the information might be brought down later. If the minister is not ready, he could give us the list a little later on. Perhaps he will tell us at the same time if any attempt was made to collect the amount of $4,600.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
Possibly the minister
could at the same time bring down a statement of what has been collected each year for the last ten years.

Item agreed to.
Registration of dipping, $3,000.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: What is this for?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
This is to defray such
costs as may be involved in the registration of Canadian shipping. Part one of the Canada Shipping Act provides that Canadian ships must be registered before engaging in trade and all the necessary facilities are provided by the Department of Marine. The expenditure is principally for printed forms and measuring appliances. As the customs officers at the ports act as registrars of shipping, no salary expenditures are involved. No change is made in the service.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: Does this apply to shipping on the Great Lakes as well as ocean shipping?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: Yes.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
Do American boats
which ply to Canadian ports have to be registered under Canadian registry?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: No.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
Was there not some
regulation last year that they had to register and file a tariff of rates with the Great Lakes' Commission?
207i

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
These vessels have not
been transferred to Canadian registry.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
They simply had tc
file their tariff of rates last year for the firs* time?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: Yes.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: Was that carried out the whole season?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
That is not under the
Department of Marine and Fisheries, but under the Department of Trade and Commerce.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
Is a registration fee
charged in those cases?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: No.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
How much was spent
last year?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE

speechtext:
Item agreed to.
Removal of obstructions in navigable waters, $5,000.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
How much was spent on
this service last year, and how much was spent in the river St. John?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
The total amount spent
was $4,972. This vote is for the removal of wrecks, not of natural obstacles.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
Under what vote is paid
the cost of removing snags in navigable rivers?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
That is under the Public
Works department.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: Is this not for the purposes of carrying out what is known as the Navigable Waters Protection Act? When a vessel is wrecked and she becomes an obstacle to navigation, the department notifies the owner to remove the obstacle, and if he does not do so, the department removes it and, if necessary, brings action against the owner to collect the costs.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: Was anything collected from the owners?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: We have made no collections.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
Has the department
got anything back for this work say in the last ten years?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: Yes.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: But nothing last year?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: Nothing last year.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
How is it that the snags are in one department and the wrecks in another?

Supply-Marine and Fisheries

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: They are not in the departments; they are in the streams.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
I cannot offer at present
any explanation. I found this situation when I took office.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
Are icebreakers used
for this work?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: No, government dredges.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: Are the icebreakers not better equipped for this work than the di edges?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
We cannot do this work
with the icebreakers. To remove obstacles from the bed) of the river we must use dredges and apparatus of that kind.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: When the minister said that he had excellent equipment I thought that possibly he meant that the department also had the necessary apparatus for removing wrecks. A question has come up regarding salaries. Is it not a fact that the officers and the crews of the vessels are given board and maintenance in addition to their wages?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: Yes.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
That is to say they
have their board and their clothing and lodging?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: Yes.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
The minister might profitably consider the wisdom of trying to get rid of duplication in these services. Something was done some time ago, but surely it would be wise to place in the hands of one department the whole work of taking care of navigation. Just imagine a dredge of the Marine department cleaning up the bed of the river after a wreck, and if there is a snag a hundred yards or so away it can do nothing but another dredge must be sent from the Public Works department to attend to that job. How absurd it really is. There would seem to be no reason why either the Marine department or the other-I do not care very much which, although I fancy the Marine department would more properly take care of this work-should not have all to do with making the river fit for navigation, no matter what the cause for the particular service may be. Dredging of every description should be done under one department, whether it be dredging in rivers or in lakes. Save for construction work, such for example as the building of a dock, which might fairly come within " public works," everything connected with navigation should come under one department. What utter waste it is to have two

departments operating two organizations in the same river, the one aiming at the snags and the other at wrecks.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
I d*o not hesitate to say
that the hon. gentleman's suggestion interests me. Undoubtedly it calls for consideration and I may say that the matter is now being studded. We hope to be able to reach a solution of it some day.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: Does the work of keeping open the ship channel in the St. Lawrence come under the Marine department or under the Department of Public Works?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: Under the Marine department?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
I am referring to the
dredges in the St. Lawrence below Montreal. Are those the dredges of the Marine department?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: Yes.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
Is it a fact that dredging
is also done in the St. Lawrence, below Montreal, by the Public Works department?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: Yes, but not in the channel.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
No, not in the channel.
But it is true that there are duplicate plants operating in the same sphere at the same time, under a double overhead and practically at double expense to the country, for capital cost and also for maintenance and operation. Is not that a fact?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
Yes; there is no doubt
that this is largely the case. But the work performed by the Marine department has to do only with the navigation channel; the work of the Department' of Public Works has nothing to do with that.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: Take dredging; would1 not that be within the province of the Department of Marine? You might dredge around a pier or a dock, but it is for the purposes of navigation. Under which department does that work come? In the city of St. John they dredge every few years the berths which fil up with silt as a result of the action of the tides. I am informed that they are dredged every year, a depth, say, of some thirty-five feet being required. Is that done by the Marine department?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
No, by the Public Works
department.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
Is not that a matter of
navigation?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
Yes, but it is local.

Supply-Marine and Fisheries

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
I d'o not understand the
principle on which this work should be done by the Public Works department while similar work is done by the Marine department in the St. Lawrence.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
The separation of these
various services as between the two departments was made several years ago.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: I suppose if the dredging were needed in a canal it would have to be done by the Railway department?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: Yes.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: Here is a great opportunity for reform on the part of the government which is hungering for exercise.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
I see good reason for
the government taking this matter into serious consideration; these services should be consolidated. There is something besides the actual dredging involved; the engineers must go to the point and inspect the works and report to the department. If there is a ship berth to be dredged at Quebec, at Montreal or at St. John the engineers of the Public Works department must first pass upon the matter; so that not only the actual dredging, but the plants which the department must maintain, and the elaborate staff of engineers to lay out the work, have all to be taken into consideration. There is therefore excellent reason why th,e government should seriously consider this proposal. And not only should they keep it under consideration; the amalgamation should actually be made.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
The minister might explain somewhat more fully this division of work as between the Marine department and the Public Works department. Some places have to shoulder the cost of this work themselves while other places have the government to fall back upon. This vote seems to apply to the ocean and river service. My hon. friend (Mr. Hanson) referred to the dredging of the St. John river; but the Great Lakes also need periodical dredging and the municipalities have to bear the cost of this -work. In the Niagara there is a very serious obstruction to navigation, and as some 2,000,000 passengers are going in and out at this point every year it is most important that the place should be dredged. Why should not the vote apply to the Great Lakes as well as to the rivers and ocean navigation? Is the Public Works department responsible for the dredging there, or is the 11 p.m. Department of Marine? I do not understand why there should be
this distinction between the two departments in this respect. Some of these votes apply only to the seaboard although the whole country has to contribute to the expenditure. Owing to the obstruction in the Niagara which I have just mentioned the steamers are obliged to make a detour, and although this obstruction has been standing for years the Public Works department will do nothing to remove it.

Item agreed to.
Inspection of live stock shipments, $4,000.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
How much was spent
last year?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: There was spent $3,416.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
At what points is the
inspection carried on?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: At Montreal, St. John and Quebec.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: Why is the vote getting larger?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
More cattle are being
shipped and we have had to provide $500 for inspection at the port of Quebec.

speakerposition: Minister of Mines; Minister of the Interior; Superintendent-General of Indian Affairs
maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
In view of the
fact that the Department of Agriculture has to undertake the inspection of cattle in order to comply with the British regulations, how does inspection come under this department?
Mr.. CARDIN:	We inspect only the fittings on the ship and make sure that it is in proper condition to carry cattle.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: Is that done to comply with the British Board of Trade regulations?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: Yes.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
There seems to me to be
a certain amount of duplication. Could not all this work be done by the same set of inspectors, as suggested by the member for Leeds (Mr. Stewart)?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
This work can be more
properly done by the inspectors of the Department of Marine and Fisheries who are in a better position to understand the condition of the ship.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: Is it not a fact that the cattle inspection is conducted by a qualified veterinary surgeon, while the inspection of the ship must be by a man qualified along different lines altogether?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
That is quite true.

Supply-Marine and Fisheries

speakerposition: Minister of Mines; Minister of the Interior; Superintendent-General of Indian Affairs
maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: Is the inspection once a year or on the occasion of every shipment?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
The boat is inspected for
every shipment.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: The inspection is required by the regulations of the British Board of Trade.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
Is it not a fact that the
Minister of Agriculture has cut off all inspection in his department except that of churches!

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: What work is actually performed by the inspector; is it merely the signing of clearance papers?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
The fittings of the vessel
are also inspected.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: I have seen ships in Montreal that were not built for cattle traffic fitted up with temporary accommodation on the upper deck, and I have known of cases where cattle have been lost as a result of these flimsy structures being washed overboard. Did our inspectors pass those ships?

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext: Yes.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
They have to pass upon

Item agreed to.
Life saving service, including rewards for saving life, $100,000.

maintopic: SUPPLY-TAX COLLECTIONS PROPOSED INQUIRY BY PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE
speechtext:
